title: probe-stream-smoothing-and-eviction-rate-limiter
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Intermittent flapping of readiness/liveness signals across our serving fleet is producing cascade autoscaler activity and aggressive pod evictions during regional capacity pressure. This manifests as repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles, increased cold-starts, transient error spikes, and ultimately SLO degradation for 95th/99th token latency and availability during regional failover.

Observed behavior: noisy readiness checks (short-lived transient failures from kernel backpressure and periodic GC pauses) are immediately translated to Kubernetes Ready=false events. The autoscaler reacts to resource signals + Ready state and triggers eviction/scale events. In cross-region failover scenarios the rapid eviction of hot KV-cache pods removes locality gains and increases inter-region traffic, prolonging recovery.

Proposal: Implement a two-part mitigation: 1) probe-stream smoothing layer in the agent that performs probabilistic decay & sticky affinity (stochastic readiness smoothing) so brief transient failures do not flip pod readiness immediately; and 2) an eviction rate limiter in the cluster controller that enforces per-node and per-availability-zone eviction windows and token-bucket rate limits tied to SLO degradation score.

Key pieces: 
- Agent-side smoothing: maintain an exponential moving average over recent probe results (configurable half-life), require sustained failure probability > threshold before marking NotReady; support override for critical liveness checks that still fail-fast.
- Sticky affinity: when a pod regains Ready, it receives a short positive affinity window that reduces preference for immediate eviction for replacement pods. This protects hot KV caches from being tossed frequently.
- Eviction rate limiter: controller-side component that tracks eviction tokens per node/zone and widens eviction windows under high SLO risk (SLO risk derived from recent 5m error-rate and p95/p99 latency deltas).
- Circuit-breaker integration: expose a circuit-breaker signal so that if SLO risk crosses critical thresholds, autoscaler policy can temporarily derate target reduction aggressiveness (shallower scale-down, hold minimum replicas).

Success criteria: reduced autoscaler thrash (scale events/min) by >= 75% in Canary trace; no SLO availability regression (target >= 99.95% P99 availability) and p99 token latency increase <= 5% vs baseline.

Tradeoffs and risks: smoothing may delay genuine failure detection (risk: hung processes). Mitigation: keep liveness checks un-smoothed by default; add explicit config flags per pod class. Eviction rate limiter introduces complexity in controller; we need to ensure it doesn't block remediation during real node failure — implement hard override for NodeNotReady with manual admin token.

Observability & testing: new dashboard tiles (scale-events/min, eviction-tokens, readiness-flap-rate, SLO-risk-index). E2E tests in staging with synthetic probe noise generator, and chaos tests simulating regional failover.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout: 1) agent smoothing default off -> enable for backend worker class in us-west1 canary for 48h; 2) enable eviction rate limiter in controller in passive mode (metrics-only) for 72h; 3) active mode in single region for 48h; 4) multi-region gradual rollout with monitoring gates and automatic rollback on SLO regression.

Artifacts: design doc, PRs, perf dashboards linked below.
acceptance_criteria: Canary shows >=75% reduction in autoscaler-driven pod churn (scale events per minute) for the target worker class
SLO availability for canary remains >= 99.95% during 72h window
p99 token latency delta <= 5% compared to pre-change baseline
Eviction rate limiter enforces configured token-bucket limits and produces telemetry in new dashboard
Feature flagging works and we can fully disable agent smoothing remotely without pod restarts
Runbook updated with new circuit-breaker and manual override steps, and on-call notified
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Triage complete. Incident linked: regional-failover-2026-02-24-postmortem. Root cause includes readiness flaps from kernel scheduler stalls + autoscaler sensitivity. Draft design created.

2026-03-02 - Luca Moretti: Design review scheduled with Platform SRE and Runtime teams. Initial concerns about delaying detection for processes stuck on GPU; recommended keeping liveness checks strict.
2026-03-03 - Priya Singh (Platform SRE): Reviewed design. Suggest adding a hard override for NodeNotReady and an emergency 'panic' flag that fully disables smoothing for a class of pods.
2026-03-04 - Engineering: Prototype agent smoothing implemented (agent/pull/1298). Local integration tests show reduced readiness flips under synthetic noise.

2026-03-05 - QA: Perf harness run in staging: autoscaler events/min dropped 82% for target workload with smoothing enabled and eviction rate limiter in passive mode. Observed small increase in detection latency for one simulated kernel hang test — acceptable due to liveness exceptions.
2026-03-06 - Security: Reviewed for potential denial-of-service where smoothing hides failure. Conclusion: acceptable with liveness exception and admin override. No further controls required.
2026-03-07 - Luca Moretti: Preparing canary rollout plan and dashboard widgets. Blocker: need kube-apiserver rate-limit exemptions for eviction token tracking (ticket raised to infra).
